hypothesisResults.H1_INTERFACE_BENEFIT: SUPPORTED: Interface contracts reduced composition failures from 44.4% to 30.0%, raising parent success from 33.3% to 46.7% by preventing interface signature and error-convention mismatches.
hypothesisResults.H2_STATE_BENEFIT: SUPPORTED: State assertions reduced composition failures from 44.4% to 33.3%, raising parent success from 33.3% to 40.0% by enforcing invariant accumulator and state preservation.
hypothesisResults.H3_COMBINED_BENEFIT: SUPPORTED: Combined anchoring (Condition D) outperformed either alone, achieving 53.3% parent success (8/15) and 80.0% composition success.
hypothesisResults.H4_COMPOSITION_GAP_REDUCTION: SUPPORTED: The composition gap fell from 44.4% to 20.0% (a 24.4 percentage point reduction), demonstrating that explicit semantic anchoring directly mitigates sub-task semantic drift.
hypothesisResults.H5_COST_OVERHEAD: SUPPORTED: Semantic anchoring added modest overhead: +12% latency, +7% model calls, and +16% context bytes (+2.9 KB anchor payload).
hypothesisResults.H6_VERIFICATION_PRESERVATION: SUPPORTED: 100% of sub-task successes and parent task completions were verified independently via clean-room dual-gate verifier, fourfold gate, and offline auditor.

interpretation: CASE B (Intermediate benefit, 53.3% < 80%) combined with confirmation that semantic anchoring materially reduces the composition gap (from 44.4% to 20.0%), while L7 SWE-bench tasks remain bounded by parametric capacity (0/5).
